{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I thought I knew constitutional law after fifteen years of practice. Then a paralegal asked why a certain precedent applied to our case. My confident explanation fell apart under her follow-up questions. I'd been citing cases without truly understanding their reasoning. Her novice perspective exposed my expert blind spots.

CANDIDATE A:
I thought I knew constitutional law after fifteen years of practice, and I was right. When a paralegal asked why a certain precedent applied to our case, I explained the doctrinal framework, the relevant holdings, and how the reasoning mapped to our facts. Her follow-up questions were good, and I could answer them all confidently. My expertise was as solid as I'd believed.

CANDIDATE B:
I've cooked my grandmother's recipes for thirty years. My daughter asked me to write them down for her. I couldn't explain why certain steps mattered—I'd just been copying her motions. Trying to articulate the cooking forced me to finally understand it.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:39"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both the SITUATION and CANDIDATE B involve a person realizing their lack of understanding in a field they thought they mastered when prompted to explain it, leading to a deeper comprehension."}
